newsitem.title: USA: Law firm files suit against Digi Int'l.
newsitem.headline: Law firm files suit against Digi Int'l.

text.p: U.S. law firm Abbey, Gardy & Squitieri LLP said Wednesday it filed a class action suit against Digi International Inc for allegedly concealing information about its financial results.

The firm said it had filed the suit the district court for the District of Minnesota on behalf of a group of investors who bought common shares in the company between January 25, 1996 and December 23, 1996.

"The Complaint charges Digi and certain of its officers and directors with violating the federal securities laws," it said. "The plaintiffs claim that defendants misrepresented and concealed material facts concerning the Company's financial results.

"The Company was improperly accounting for Digi's investment in Aetherworks and had engaged in special promotions, including extended payment terms to distributors, in order to artificially inflate the Company's reported earnings," it added.
Jonathon Killmer, the company's chief financial officer, said the suit was the same as three others filed against Digi since the beginning of the year.
"And we have referred them all to counsel," he said, declining to comment further.
In January, firms Wolf Popper LLP and Lockridge Grindal Nauen & Holstein LLP filed a similar suit against the company.
Digi's stock fell below $9 on December 24 after it revised downward its fiscal 1996 earnings and forecast weaker first quarter profits. Its stock had been trading at a high of $30 before the fall.
On Wednesday, it was trading at $8-1/8.
